doc.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016

title: Playing into old age, Snooky Young and Joe Wilder
summary: Jenkins expects to keep playing longer than teaching, citing Snooky Young and Joe Wilder, and wants to play newer music as he ages.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I know. But well we were just talking about Joe Wilder. And I was introduced to him by Snooky Young. And Snooky and I were together in the Clayton-Hamilton band for 26 years. And he lived to be 90. He played until he passed away. And I just saw how young it kept him. And my dad played and it kept him young. Unless I get to where I can’t play very well you know. But I still feel like I’m really sort of — I feel like there’s a lot more music I want to write and a lot more music I want to play. And I don’t know where I’ll be. I may be on the west coast or I may be in New York, I don’t know where I’ll be. But I do feel like I’ll be playing.
Okay. You could do a Doc Cheatham.
Well you know that’s the thing. I don’t want to do that either.
I don’t want to play older music. I want to play newer music when I’m older.

Well, and I want to play well. I don’t want to play okay. And trumpets are very physical athletic sort of things. So that may dictate how long I play. Snooky didn’t hear very well in his last years — he didn’t hear very well and that hampered his playing a bit, but he still played very well.
That’s the same with Joe I think. He had the hearing aid thing, but he certainly had a marvelous conception.

Yeah. I met him and he was playing with the Carnegie — no, no, — he was playing with the Smithsonian. And I met him in Europe one time. Snooky introduced me to him. What a gentleman he was, wow. What a marvelous guy.
